questions.question_text: In modern JavaScript (ES6+), what is the primary operational difference between 'Promise.all()' and 'Promise.allSettled()'?

options.text: Promise.all() rejects immediately if any promise rejects, while Promise.allSettled() waits for all promises to resolve or reject.
Promise.allSettled() runs promises in sequential order, while Promise.all() runs in parallel.
Promise.all() only accepts synchronous functions, whereas Promise.allSettled() accepts async functions.
There is no difference; Promise.allSettled() is just an alias for Promise.all().
